summary: Join our Ecosystem Services Valuation Training Course to learn how to assess and value nature's benefits. Empower your career and protect the environment.
lede: Ecosystem services valuation helps project and policy professionals assess how nature supports people and affects decisions. Designed for people who shape land use, conservation, climate and development work, the course covers identifying and classifying ecosystem services, measuring them with biophysical indicators and available data, and choosing monetary or non-monetary valuation approaches. Participants also practice comparing project options, weighing uncertainty and trade-offs, and communicating results to stakeholders.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who regularly make or influence decisions that affect ecosystems, land use, and natural capital.
audience: Planners and policy officers in ministries
NGO and civil society program managers
Climate, biodiversity, and resilience project leads
Corporate sustainability, ESG, and CSR managers
Impact investment and development finance professionals
Agriculture, forestry, and water resource managers
Environmental economists, analysts, and M&E professionals interested
modules: Economic Valuation Methods for Ecosystem Services
Integrating Ecosystem Services into Project and Policy Appraisal
Ecosystem Services in Public, NGO, and Corporate Programs
Biases, Uncertainty, and Ethical Issues in Valuation
Ecosystem Services, Risk, and Climate Resilience
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of environmental management concepts and experience in project or policy development. Familiarity with economic principles and sustainability practices is beneficial but not essential.
